fields.why: The data are a prospective program cohort of Russian TB patients: the brief's shortcut sends all international data to 'international surveillance' (A), but they are study/program records rather than surveillance, so 'other' (B) is also defensible. A rule for non-surveillance international study data would decide it.
The brief says age is recorded always; the article reports 'Mean age at diagnosis was 40 years', which B left out.

The article cites mandatory biannual prison screening (a policy) to explain prisoners' better outcomes, and lack of TB-symptom education to explain high fatality, so determinants are named; A's 'Russian TB control traditions' item is weaker because it explains physicians' slow adoption of DOTS, not an outcome.

brief_issues: The 'international surveillance' shortcut does not cover international prospective study or program-cohort data; the determinants rule does not say whether a screening policy named as the reason for one group's better outcomes counts.
